doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Early bands and Luis Russell's Harlem
title: Charlie Holmes recommends him to Luis Russell, 1945
summary: Holmes told Russell about him; Haynes accepted by telegram after a summer gig on Martha's Vineyard, with pay and uniforms discussed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Not immediately, because I went to Connecticut to play for a while. That’s where I met this alto saxophonist Charlie Holmes, whom had played with Louis Armstrong and Luis Russell. He told Luis Russell about me. Luis Russell had never heard me. He sent me a special delivery letter. We were playing at Martha’s Vineyard, part of Cape Cod there.
With - when you say “we,” who was with you?

I was still with Phil Edmond. I did send him back a telegram. I told him I was interested in joining the band, but I couldn’t join until after Labor Day, because that was a summer gig that we had. Then I come to New York.
So you started out making 12 bucks a week playing in a trio. Then how much were you making by the time you were getting ready to leave Phil Edmond?
I don’t know what it was then. It was much more though, but I don’t remember. I guess I remember that 12 because it was my first weekly salary playing drums.
I was just trying to get a feel for what the fees were like back in those days.
A summer gig. I don’t know if it was 25 or what. Maybe.
And traveling. Were you doing much?
We would travel from Boston to New Hampshire and then drive back. If we had a couple of gigs we’d stay over somewhere.
Did you have band uniforms? Do you remember if you had . . .?
Good question. I don’t remember. They must have. But a lot of those – in Boston, a lot of times naturally it would be black suit, black tie. That was traditional.
So now it’s after Labor Day. What year?
